Automotive / Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Inspected stock listed everywhere, and paperwork that closes on time

Used-vehicle businesses live on sourcing good stock, pricing it right, listing it fast and transferring ownership cleanly. We connect evaluation, inventory, marketplace listings and Vahan paperwork so every vehicle has one record, honest condition notes and a tracked transfer from the previous owner to the next.

The challenge

What makes pre-owned vehicle dealers different.

01

Evaluation requests from sellers and exchange customers arrive by phone and WhatsApp, and evaluators travel without the RC details, photos or service history they need.

02

Listings on the website and several marketplaces drift out of sync, so sold vehicles stay listed and price changes reach some portals and not others.

03

Condition, ownership count and accident or flood history are described differently by each salesperson, which invites disputes after the sale.

04

Ownership transfer, hypothecation removal and other-state NOCs depend on documents from sellers, lenders and buyers, and delays leave liability unclear while the RC still shows the previous owner.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for pre-owned vehicle dealers.

01

Seller and exchange evaluation booking

Sellers share registration number, model year, kilometers and photos in a WhatsApp flow, pick a doorstep or yard inspection slot and receive an offer only after the evaluator and manager have reviewed the vehicle.

02

Inspection-led listings

Listing text drafted from the structured inspection report and approved by the used-car manager, then published to the website and marketplace dealer panels from one inventory record.

03

Stock aging and price review

A daily view of days in stock, refurbishment status, enquiries per listing and price changes, so managers review slow stock with facts instead of guesses.

04

Transfer document tracker

Form 29C intimation, Forms 29 and 30, Form 35 and the lender NOC for financed vehicles, and Form 28 NOCs for other states, tracked per vehicle with reminders to whoever owes the next document.

05

Trip log for stock vehicles

Test drives and workshop runs logged with purpose, driver, time and odometer reading, ready for the electronic trip register the CMVR rules require of registered-vehicle dealers.

06

Post-sale care

Feedback after delivery and a tracked response to condition or warranty complaints, so issues are handled before they become public reviews.

Automation blueprints

The automations we would start with.

Discover and enquireStandard3–5 weeks

Instant lead response, qualification and routing

Leads from OEM portals, the website, ad lead forms, marketplaces, missed calls and WhatsApp are deduplicated, acknowledged within minutes where the buyer has opted in, qualified with a short flow and assigned to a consultant with a first-call timer.

New vehicle dealerships · Pre-owned vehicle dealers · EV & two-wheeler dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Dealerships pay for leads from several sources, but each source has its own portal and inbox. Leads that arrive after hours or during busy showroom periods wait, duplicates are called twice by different consultants, and buyers who hear nothing soon enquire at the next dealership.

Trigger

A new lead arrives from an OEM lead portal export or API, a website form, Meta or Google lead forms, a marketplace dealer panel, an IVR missed call or a click-to-WhatsApp chat.

How it runs

  • Normalize the lead, match the mobile number against open DMS or CRM enquiries and merge duplicates, keeping every source for attribution.
  • Check the consent captured on the source form; opted-in buyers receive an approved WhatsApp template, and everyone else becomes a call task.
  • Run a short WhatsApp flow for model, variant or fuel, purchase timeframe, exchange and finance interest, and classify free-text questions without answering price or offer questions.
  • Assign the lead by brand, branch, model and language, create or update the enquiry in the DMS or CRM and start a first-call timer.
  • Alert the team leader in Slack when the timer lapses, and reassign after a second lapse under the rules the sales manager sets.
  • Log source, response times and outcome for the weekly lead review.

Human checkpoint

The sales consultant makes the first call and answers anything about price, discounts, exchange value or finance. Team leaders handle reassignment, and the sales manager approves templates, qualifying questions and routing rules before launch and after every change.

Discover and enquireStandard4–6 weeks

Inspection-led listings synced to the website and marketplaces

Once a vehicle passes inspection and refurbishment, listing text is drafted from the structured inspection report, approved by the used-car manager and published to the website and marketplace dealer panels from one record. Reserved and sold vehicles come down everywhere.

Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Listings are typed separately into each portal, so descriptions vary, price changes reach some portals and not others, and sold cars keep attracting calls. Condition details depend on who wrote the listing, which leads to disputes after the sale.

Trigger

A vehicle's status changes to ready for sale, reserved, sold or repriced in the used-vehicle inventory record.

How it runs

  • Pull the vehicle record: make, model, variant, year, odometer reading as recorded, ownership count, inspection findings and photos.
  • Draft listing text from those fields only, with no claim that the inspection report does not support, and flag any missing disclosure.
  • Route the draft, price and disclosures to the used-car manager for approval in the console.
  • Publish to the dealer website and to each marketplace through the dealer feed, API or bulk upload template it offers, or prepare the listing for manual posting where it offers none, and record each listing ID.
  • On reservation, sale or repricing, update or remove the listing on every channel, and send each marketplace's leads into the lead queue.

Human checkpoint

The used-car manager approves price, condition notes and disclosures such as accident, flood or repaint history before anything is published. Pricing suggestions are never applied automatically.

Test drive and evaluationStandard3–5 weeks

Seller and exchange evaluation booking

Owners who want to sell or exchange share vehicle details and photos in a short WhatsApp flow, book a yard or doorstep inspection and receive an offer only after an evaluator has inspected the vehicle and a manager has approved the price.

Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Sell-my-car enquiries and exchange requests arrive by call and chat with incomplete details. Evaluators travel without the RC, service history or photos they need, and offers given over the phone before an inspection are later revised, which frustrates sellers.

Trigger

A seller enquiry arrives from the website, a marketplace or WhatsApp, or a new-vehicle consultant flags an exchange request in the CRM.

How it runs

  • Collect registration number, model, year, kilometers driven, ownership count, loan status and photos through a WhatsApp flow.
  • Offer yard or doorstep slots by evaluator and area, and send reminders listing the documents to keep ready.
  • Give the evaluator a structured inspection checklist in an app, with photos and findings saved against the vehicle.
  • Show the manager the inspection report, the evaluator's recommendation and comparable recent purchases from your own records.
  • Send the approved offer with its validity period, and pass accepted vehicles to purchase and transfer paperwork.

Human checkpoint

The evaluator inspects every vehicle in person, and the used-car manager approves each offer price. No automated price is ever quoted to a seller.

Quote, finance and bookingAdvanced5–7 weeks

On-road quote with finance and insurance desk handoff

Consultants issue consistent on-road quotes from approved price lists and insurer quotes, with optional items shown as clear opt-ins. Finance and insurance requests move to the F&I desk with the buyer's consent, and lender disclosures and decisions stay with the lender.

New vehicle dealerships · Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Quotes are typed from price sheets, so one buyer can get different figures from different consultants, optional accessories look mandatory and discount approvals happen on calls. Finance interest is passed to lender executives on chat without consent or tracking, and nobody can see why a booking is waiting on the loan.

Trigger

A consultant marks a quote as requested in the CRM or DMS after a test drive or a pricing enquiry.

How it runs

  • Assemble the quote from the approved price list, the state registration and road tax table, an insurer quote and selected accessories, with an issue date and validity period.
  • Show accessories, extended warranty and add-on covers as separate optional lines the buyer chooses, never preselected.
  • Route discounts or exchange bonuses above the consultant's limit to the sales manager for approval before the quote is sent.
  • Send the quote as a secure link and record its version against the enquiry.
  • On request and with consent, share the minimum details with the buyer's chosen lender through its DSA or sourcing channel, and track status to sanction and disbursal.
  • Hand insurance to the dealership's designated insurance executive, log the insurer, cover and add-ons the buyer chooses, and record when the buyer arranges cover elsewhere.

Human checkpoint

The sales manager approves discounts and exchange values above limits. The lender makes every credit decision and issues its Key Facts Statement; the dealership shows EMIs only as indicative. The designated insurance executive explains cover and add-ons, and the buyer chooses the insurer and cover.

Allotment, paperwork and deliveryStandard4–5 weeks

Ownership transfer and RC document tracker for used vehicles

Every vehicle bought or sold gets a transfer file covering Form 29C intimation, Forms 29 and 30, hypothecation removal and NOCs, with reminders to whoever owes the next document and alerts before statutory reporting windows close.

Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

A used vehicle passes from seller to dealer to buyer, often with a loan to close, an NOC from another state and documents from three parties. When files stall, the RC still shows the previous owner, liability is unclear and buyers chase the dealer for months.

Trigger

A purchase from a seller or a sale to a buyer is closed in the used-vehicle DMS or inventory record.

How it runs

  • Open a transfer file recording the vehicle, the parties, any loan, the state of registration and the acknowledgment number of the Form 29C intimation signed by owner and dealer on Vahan.
  • Generate the document checklist for the case, such as Forms 29 and 30, Form 35 and the lender NOC for financed vehicles, a Form 28 NOC for other-state transfers, insurance and PUC.
  • Check for pending challans, lapsed insurance or PUC and open hypothecation, collect documents through secure links, and record the documentation executive's verification of each item.
  • Remind whoever owes the next document, and alert the manager as the seller's and buyer's reporting windows under Section 50 of the Motor Vehicles Act approach.
  • Update the buyer when the Vahan application is filed and when the new RC is issued, and prompt the insurance transfer to the new owner.

Human checkpoint

The documentation executive checks identities and signatures and files every application on Vahan; the automation only tracks and reminds. The used-car manager handles exceptions such as pending challans, lender delays or disputes.

Feedback, renewals and upgradeStandard3–4 weeks

Post-delivery and post-service feedback with service recovery

A short feedback request follows each delivery and service visit. Low ratings, repeat concerns and complaints become tickets with the job or sale history attached, and a named person calls the owner back within the agreed time.

Service centres & workshops · Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Dealerships collect ratings, often for OEM surveys, but unhappy owners rarely get a call. Repeat repairs and post-sale complaints about used vehicles surface first in public reviews or consumer complaints instead of on a manager's desk.

Trigger

A vehicle is handed over after a sale or a service visit, and the delivery or gate pass is closed in the DMS.

How it runs

  • Wait the agreed interval, then send one or two questions and an optional comment box.
  • Classify comments by theme, such as delay, billing, workmanship, staff or vehicle condition, and summarize them for the ticket.
  • Open a ticket for low ratings, complaints or a repeat visit for the same concern within the agreed period, with the job card or sale details attached.
  • Assign the call-back to the customer relations manager, and to the works manager or used-car manager for workmanship or condition issues.
  • Track call-back, resolution and any goodwill decision, and report themes monthly by advisor, workshop and model.

Human checkpoint

The customer relations manager calls every flagged owner, and the works manager or used-car manager decides on rework, refunds or goodwill. Staff never ask owners to change or inflate OEM survey ratings.

Tools

Systems it connects
